rows.why_it_might_help: Could finally train addressing on "did this card help?". But use top-1, not top-4 (top-4 still delivers distractors), and one checkpoint already shows recall@4 = 1.0 with 60/1024 accuracy, so selection is not always the bottleneck.
rows.cheapest_test: Free first: log recall@k on existing checkpoints. Then, on own-retrieval (not the supplied-card ladder), one sampling arm vs an identical-seed, identical-data, CE-only control, 3 seeds.
rows.cost: GPU-hours; needs a CPU-to-GPU port first
rows.relation_to_current_plan: Competes with H1 pool controls for the same diagnosis

rows.idea: Reset the decoder periodically (iterated learning)
rows.targets: Seed instability (503/512 vs 27/512) and no regularisation anywhere in the reasoner
rows.what_it_is: Every N steps re-initialise the decoder only, keeping reader, writer and Think, so any card code the writer invents has to stay quickly re-learnable by a fresh decoder.
rows.why_it_might_help: Aims at variance rather than the mean; a tight band would restore trust in nearly every toy conclusion. Evidence is a referential game with tiny message spaces, and the detailed numbers are unverified beyond the abstract.
rows.cheapest_test: Run the cheaper control first: a 3-seed cosine-decay rerun of bypass-k1 at 1500 steps. If decay alone tightens the band, drop this. Pre-register the spread metric.
rows.relation_to_current_plan: New; prerequisite for trusting any toy A/B result

rows.idea: Matrix-valued recurrent state for recall capacity
rows.targets: The reader's small vector state (d=32 in real runs) cannot hold identity and value together
rows.what_it_is: Give each head a small matrix state (say four 8x8 heads, 256 numbers) instead of one 32-number vector, because in-context recall capacity tracks state size.
rows.why_it_might_help: At d=32 the capacity argument is compelling. Counter-evidence first: probes already decode person and value 2304/2304 at the key token positions, so test this on the long-range own-retrieval path, not on pooling.
rows.cheapest_test: Build an MQAR-style probe from village data at N = 4, 8, 16, 32; vector-state control vs matrix state, 3 seeds. Drop the idea if both degrade identically.
rows.relation_to_current_plan: Extends the reader fix in g64; upstream of pooling

rows.idea: Report four efficiency axes, not one
rows.targets: One FLOP axis carries the efficiency claim, and the counter skips the scan's elementwise work
rows.what_it_is: Report every arm on accuracy per training token, per counted FLOP, and per isolated GPU second, and state plainly which axis the claim rests on.
rows.why_it_might_help: No accuracy change, a defensibility change. Accuracy-per-parameter adds nothing (config already forces all D variants into one narrow band), and seconds should wait until the scan is profiled, or an unoptimised loop kills a good design.
rows.cheapest_test: Post-process checkpoints already on disk into three columns plus one isolated timing pass each. The check is whether any arm's ranking changes between columns; if all agree, the old claim stands.
rows.cost: Minutes of GPU timing; otherwise free
rows.relation_to_current_plan: Extends adopted FLOP-parity; applies across all experiments

rows.idea: Score each loop on what the last one missed
rows.targets: Think loop: no evidence later loops add anything; per-(question,loop) loss normalisation
rows.what_it_is: Keep deep supervision but weight each loop's answer loss by how often the previous loop got that question wrong — boosting inside the recurrence. No new parameters.
rows.why_it_might_help: Today the cheapest solution is an answer already right at loop 1 and unchanged after; weighting gives later loops a reason to exist. The cited papers are decorative, not evidence.
rows.cheapest_test: Free first: log accuracy-by-loop and alpha on existing checkpoints. Then alpha init 0.1 vs 0.0, then per-question normalisation; error-weighting only if loops differ. Control: uniform supervision.
rows.relation_to_current_plan: New; prerequisite for any honest claim about the think loop

rows.idea: Sparse knowledge slots written only in sleep
rows.targets: No retention or continual-learning number exists; store is episode-scoped, no cross-visit knowledge
rows.what_it_is: Replace one feed-forward block in the 4M Core model with a large key-value slot table, and when learning new facts update only the few slots those facts activate.
rows.why_it_might_help: Published NaturalQuestions F1 drop: 89% full finetune, 71% LoRA, 11% slot-sparse. But all evidence is 0.5B+; at 4M from scratch slots may never learn keys, and selection needs usage history.
rows.cheapest_test: Train village 1; learn village 2 updating only top-activated slots, dense weights frozen. Controls: full finetune, and slot layer with all parameters trained. Decide parameter counting first.
rows.relation_to_current_plan: New; first retention evidence, run after pool controls

rows.idea: Offline re-reading pass instead of harder thinking
rows.targets: Dead Think gates (alpha 0.018-0.042); card content, with held-out two-hop secondary
rows.what_it_is: Instead of thinking harder while answering, re-run the reader over the visit two or four extra times offline, feeding each pass's card values back in, then answer.
rows.why_it_might_help: A 2026 paper at this exact scale (4 layers, d=256, from scratch) found more offline passes help most on deeper multi-hop. Its fast-weight mechanism is rejected here; only 're-reading helps' transfers.
rows.cheapest_test: Free checks first: alpha init 0.1 and residual_std/sqrt(max_loops). Then N=1 (control) vs 2 vs 4 matched on wall-clock, since the FLOP counter misses minGRU. Three seeds.
rows.relation_to_current_plan: Competes with the planned bounded reread of selected evidence

rows.idea: Screen the sleep idea cheaply before building it
rows.targets: Unbuilt sleep-as-transaction; no regulariser anywhere; large seed-to-seed spread
rows.what_it_is: A short offline phase every N steps that shrinks all weights toward baseline, replays a small buffer, and commits only if validation did not worsen — otherwise rolls back.
rows.why_it_might_help: It would be the first regulariser and builds the rollback harness the vision needs. But the newest evidence says the same intervention gives no measurable benefit under gradient training, so expect a null.
rows.cheapest_test: Precommitted screen: sleep ratio 0% (control), 10%, 20%, 30% on the standard 600 s Core run, three seeds. Snapshot model, AdamW state and RNG together, or results are noise.
rows.relation_to_current_plan: New; harness is reusable, the shrink is a screen

rows.idea: J-lens readability for Premonition-mini
rows.targets: No mid-thought readability tool; do Think loops change anything; does a card carry person
rows.what_it_is: Average the Jacobian from the decoder's answer logits back to each think row over a few hundred visits, then print any row as the answer tokens it is poised to say.
rows.why_it_might_help: Would give a loop-by-loop transcript. But Premonition's decoder is one block, so the averaged Jacobian is nearly exact — in practice this is a cross-attention-corrected logit lens, useful but modest.
rows.cheapest_test: On an existing checkpoint, 200 held-out visits: does the lens's top token on the gold-card row predict the model's first answer token better than a plain logit lens and a distractor row?
rows.relation_to_current_plan: New tooling; would support pool controls and H1 diagnosis

rows.idea: Meta-learn what a question wants from examples
rows.targets: Held-out wording collapse: Q6 62.4% to 1.1%, Q11 28.8% to 0.0%
rows.what_it_is: Put one or two same-type questions, worded differently and with their answers, earlier in the same visit, then ask the target question in an unseen phrasing.
rows.why_it_might_help: Attacks the measured failure directly — answering in the wrong answer space. Minnow shows from-scratch child-scale models can learn this. Risk: in-visit answers leak; the audit already flags 64 cases.
rows.cheapest_test: Must run on the Core village track, not the toy ladder, which has one surface form per type. Matched 600 s runs at k=0/1/2 demos; control: demos shuffled across types.
rows.cost: 5070 Ti 600 s per arm; several arms
rows.relation_to_current_plan: New; gated on first adding more training phrasings

rows.idea: Oracle-checked dreams: verified self-generated replay
rows.targets: Unbuilt dream replay; no backward-transfer number for the adopted diary replay
rows.what_it_is: Let the model generate its own practice material at a village boundary, have the exact village oracle mark it, and train only on the parts that pass.
rows.why_it_might_help: Self-generated replay nearly eliminated forgetting in a 2026 study, and Premonition uniquely owns a checker. But at 23% held-out accuracy most dreams fail, and filtering entrenches what the model already knows.
rows.cheapest_test: Run no-replay vs exact 50:50 diary replay first. Then dream only question-answer pairs about visits already seen (no visit parser exists) and gate on the oracle acceptance rate.
rows.relation_to_current_plan: New; needs a continual-learning harness built first

rows.idea: Multiplicative (HRR) binding inside the card
rows.targets: One pooled card cannot hold person, relation and value; binder writes the same value everywhere
rows.what_it_is: Build the card as a sum of role-times-filler products (circular convolution), so 'who', 'relation' and 'value' can each be pulled back out by correlating with its role vector.
rows.why_it_might_help: A principled way to hold several fields in one vector. But capacity scales with dimension and the toy runs at d=32, where three superposed pairs likely become unreadable; past probes found answers card-blind anyway.
rows.cheapest_test: Seconds on the Mac first: at d=32 and d=128, how accurately does unbinding recover each filler, scored as cleanup against the toy's actual small vocabularies? If d=32 fails, stop.
rows.cost: Mac seconds to screen; GPU only if passed
rows.relation_to_current_plan: Competes with H1 binding fixes; successor to slice binding

rows.idea: Different clocks for different modules
rows.targets: Card writer is 1.2% of params and loses the pooling race; seed instability
rows.what_it_is: Give the card writer its own slower clock — cleanest as an EMA slow copy of its parameters — while the reader and decoder keep updating every step.
rows.why_it_might_help: Tests the vision's 'weights change only in sleep' on one module for the price of a schedule change. But slowing both competing gradients equally is a weak fix, and no citation tests it.
rows.cheapest_test: Add as one extra arm inside the pool-controls run: K=1 (control) vs a slow EMA writer, three seeds. Precommit seed spread as the primary number; specify Adam state handling.
rows.cost: 5070 Ti minutes; extra arm, no new run
rows.relation_to_current_plan: Extends pool controls as a cheap extra arm

rows.idea: One phrasing per batch
rows.targets: Held-out question wording is the Core track's next wall; no per-phrasing batching
rows.what_it_is: Make each batch use a single phrasing instead of mixing phrasings, so gradients from different wordings stop averaging into a compromise that suits none of them.
rows.why_it_might_help: A 2026 head-to-head lifted worst-template score from 0.210 to 0.363 and beat the paraphrase-agreement loss Ben plans to build. But those were instruction-tuned 0.6-8B models that already knew the task.
rows.cheapest_test: Not free: a training row is a whole visit with about nine mixed questions, so this needs regenerating data with one phrasing per visit. Then two matched 600 s runs; report worst phrasing per type.
rows.cost: Data regeneration plus two 600 s runs
rows.relation_to_current_plan: Informs whether to build the planned paraphrase-agreement loss
